title: West Berkshire Council: Development of generative AI tools
summary: West Berkshire Council reports that its job-advert generator, built on OpenAI GPT models, reduced managers' drafting time and made adverts more consistent.
account: West Berkshire used GPT-based tools to generate job advertisements and explored internal and public-information assistants. Managers report less drafting time and more consistent formatting. The source reports roughly £300 in setup staff time and £2 in monthly running costs. Recycling and policy assistants were planned, and their benefits had not been established. On 19 February 2024 the chief executive of GOSS, the council's platform supplier, wrote that the council's digital services manager had described the job-advert tool at a UKA Live panel. According to that account, the manager said that the cost per use was small but that the results were variable, ranked around B-, and needed human checks.
purpose: Reduce work drafting recruitment material and explore customized assistants for council information.
system: Custom job-advert generator using OpenAI GPT models and the ChatGPT API; other assistant prototypes

developer: West Berkshire Council using OpenAI models
